title_s: The Production of Steatite Beads and Ornaments at Chanhu-daro during the first centuries of the Indus Civilization. An Insight into a specialized workshop area discovered In Mound I
abstract_s: One of the most remarkable results of the excavation-season 2024 at Chanhu-daro, carried out by the French Archaeological Mission in the Indus Basin in cooperation with the Directorate General of Antiquities and Archaeology, Government of Sindh, is the discovery of a workshop area totally dedicated to steatite working. This specialized production area was unearthed in the eastern slope of Mound I (Trench 6-East) and contrasts with the other multi-material” lapidary workshops uncovered in 2017-2019 in Excavation 2 (Mound II). The mudbrick building excavated in Mound I belongs to several architectural phases ascribed to the end of the 1st Indus period (2600/2500-2300 BCE) based on stratigraphic and ceramic studies, and it was specifically designed for the development of this craft production. It includes various rooms for the steatite treatment and firing in specific installations that have left numerous remains. The number of artifacts discovered in this building is considerable. The studies carried out to date have made possible to define that certain materials were processed in specific areas of the site, and to specify various technical processes. The combination of these results gives us a detailed methodological picture of stone bead production and the socioeconomic organization at Chanhu-daro, as demonstrated by the steatite workshops excavated in 2024 in Trench 6-East.

Since 2023, the MAFBI programme focuses on Mound I, little-investigated in the 1930s, with the objective to document the complete occupation sequence of Chanhu-daro covering the entire urban period (2600/2500-1900 BCE) and the post-Indus period (2nd millennium BCE).

title_s: French Archaeological Mission in the Indus Basin. Excavations at Chanhu-daro and explorations in Sindh, Field-Season 2024. Final Report
